# local 0006: mcs51: Branching Range Exceeded after peephole rule 257.c replaces sjmp by ljmp between a short jump and its label

- Category: [Problems without a ticket](../../unreported.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Give rule 257.c a condition that keeps the short jumps across its place in range, or remove the rule.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The file below does not assemble. It was compiled on r17176 with `sdcc -mmcs51 -c r2.c`, and the
assembler reports `r2.asm:219: Error: <a> Branching Range Exceeded.` Line 219 is `jb _bt,00115$`,
the jump at the end of the loop. In the listing the label is at 0x0007 and the `jb` instruction
ends at 0x0089. That is 130 bytes, and the range is 128.

```c
#define CASE(n) case n: bt2 = 1; break;
#define FN8 fn (); fn (); fn (); fn (); fn (); fn (); fn (); fn ();

volatile __bit bt, bt2;
volatile unsigned char g;
void fn (void);

void h (unsigned char x, unsigned char y) __reentrant
{
  do
    {
      if (y)
        {
          switch (x)
            {
            CASE (3) CASE (13) CASE (23) CASE (33) CASE (43) CASE (53)
            CASE (63) CASE (73) CASE (83) CASE (93) CASE (103)
            }
          return;
        }
      g = 20;
      g = 21;
      g = 22;
    }
  while (bt);
  FN8 FN8 FN8 FN8 FN8
}
```

With `--no-peep` the file assembles. The failure depends on the size of the loop. With four
`g = n;` statements the jump stays long and the file assembles. With two of them it assembles
with the small model and fails with `--model-medium`, `--model-large`, `--model-huge`, and
`--model-large --stack-auto`, where the statements are longer.

## Cause

Each `break` is a jump to the label of the `return` statement, `00112$`, and the code there is a
jump to the epilogue at `00118$`, which is out of `sjmp` range. The function has an epilogue
because it is `__reentrant` and has a parameter on the stack. With `--fverbose-asm` the assembly
names the rules that were applied. Rule 112.b replaces each `ljmp 00112$` by `sjmp 00112$`. Rules
112.b and 108.e replace the `jnb` and `ljmp` at the end of the loop by `jb _bt,00115$`, after
`labelInRange` has found the label in range. Rule 257.c then replaces `sjmp 00112$` by
`ljmp 00118$` in ten places, and each replacement adds 1 byte. Without these 10 bytes the `jb` is
120 bytes from its label.

The order was read from the source. `peepHole` in `src/SDCCpeeph.c` applies each rule to all
lines before it tries the next rule, and rules 112.b and 108.e are in front of the 257 group in
`src/mcs51/peeph.def`. Rule 257.b replaces `sjmp %5` by `sjmp %6` when `labelInRange(%6)` holds.
Rule 257.c applies to the `sjmp %5` that remain and has no range condition. It is the only rule
of the 257 group that changes the size of a jump. No rule checks the `jb` again.

r16761 changed the replacement of this rule from `sjmp %6` to `ljmp %6` and removed its
`labelInRange(%6)`. r16836 added the `sjmp` form again as 257.b and gave the `ljmp` form the
number 257.c.

## Related

Bug #3843 reports this assembler message for another cause. Its two patches do not change
`src/mcs51/peeph.def`.
